name: What if my open-concept kitchen conversion hits an unexpected structural problem?

mainEntity.name: What happens if demolition reveals a structural issue during an open-concept kitchen conversion?
mainEntity.text: What happens if demolition reveals a structural issue during an open-concept kitchen conversion?

acceptedAnswer.text: Unexpected structural issues are one of the biggest risks in open-concept conversions. Once the wall is opened, the team may discover damaged framing, undersized supports, hidden beams, past modifications, termite or water damage, or load conditions that were not obvious during planning. When that happens, the job may need revised engineering, new materials, permit updates, and extra inspection steps. It can also extend the schedule because the work cannot safely continue until the structure is resolved. The smartest way to manage this risk is to build contingency into the budget and insist on a thorough preconstruction review. In older Los Angeles homes, surprises are common enough that a good estimate should assume some unknowns. A contractor should explain what happens if the scope changes mid-project and how decisions are approved before extra work proceeds. That protects both the structure and the budget.
acceptedAnswer.description: If hidden framing, damaged supports, or unplanned load conditions appear during demolition, the project may need revised engineering, added support, schedule changes, and extra cost. That is why contingency budget and preconstruction inspection matter before wall removal begins.
